questions.cardText:
[Botany] What is the oldest viable seed on record?
A. Wheat seed from an ancient Egyptian tomb
B. Lotus seed from a Chinese lakebed
C. Date palm seed from Masada, Israel
Answer: C. A date palm seed discovered at the ancient fortress of Masada was successfully germinated after nearly 2,000 years. This remarkable achievement demonstrated the incredible longevity of seeds under the right conditions.
questions.de: Von welcher Pflanze stammte der rund 2000 Jahre alte Samen aus der antiken Festung Masada, den israelische Forscher 2005 zum Keimen brachten?
questions.en: From which plant was the roughly 2,000-year-old seed, found at the ancient fortress of Masada, that Israeli scientists germinated in 2005?

timeline.labelEn: Israeli scientists germinate a 2,000-year-old Judean date palm seed from Masada; the sapling is named Methuselah
timeline.labelDe: Israelische Forscher bringen einen 2000 Jahre alten Samen der Judäischen Dattelpalme aus Masada zum Keimen; der Setzling heißt Methusalem

questions.notes: Card overstates: Wikipedia calls it the oldest seed germinated with human assistance; Silene stenophylla plants were regenerated (2012) from ~32,000-year-old fruit tissue in Siberian permafrost, so 'oldest viable seed' is debatable. Question asks the plant instead.

questions.cardText:
[Earth Science] Where is the largest temperate rainforest in the world?
A. Alaska, U.S.A.
B. Hokkaido, Japan
C. Yunnan, China
Answer: A. Tongass National Forest in Alaska is the largest temperate rainforest in the world.
questions.de: In welchem US-Bundesstaat liegt der Tongass National Forest, der oft als größter gemäßigter Regenwald der Welt bezeichnet wird?
questions.en: In which U.S. state is the Tongass National Forest, often called the world's largest temperate rainforest?

timeline.labelEn: Theodore Roosevelt proclaims the Tongass National Forest in Southeast Alaska
timeline.labelDe: Theodore Roosevelt ruft den Tongass National Forest im Südosten Alaskas aus

questions.notes: Wikipedia: the largest US national forest, mostly temperate rainforest, 'one of the biggest intact temperate rainforests'; the 'world's largest' claim is common but loose (the whole Pacific coastal temperate rainforest belt is larger).
